Side note for the architect, out of this row's scope: apps/daemon/src/http/document-ingest-route.ts:4-5 asserts ADMIN is "the one capability an agent session scoped to WORK, GOAL or PLANNING never holds" and gates on it at :140, while agentCapabilitiesFor grants [ADMIN, WORK] to three agent kinds; same fence shape, separate finding.

THIRD HUMAN REVIEW of PR #3 (anchored at d01c3316), P1 merge blocker R3-1, reviewer's words: "An ADMIN agent can self-approve pairing and escalate into a renewable five-capability session. Pairing approval checks only project membership and project.admin, despite the codebase stating ADMIN fences reach, not human authority (apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-pairing-routes.ts:151-169; apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:95-104). A scoped ADMIN agent can request pairing, approve its own label, claim it, and receive ADMIN, GOAL, PLANNING, REVIEW, WORK for 12 hours (apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts:298-312). Require the configured operator principal, or remove authenticated HTTP approval and retain terminal-only approval."

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD a09b11fa (19 commits after d01c3316): STILL PRESENT, byte-identical. http-listener-pairing-routes.ts approveAuthenticated() :151-170 admits on :159 projectId match and :162 `principal.capabilities.includes(CAPABILITIES.ADMIN)` only, then :168 calls approvalWindow.operator.approve(label); no principalId comparison exists in the file. Route is live at http-listener.ts:676-687. Request/claim routes (:213-246) are unauthenticated by design. Escalation chain: session-authenticator.ts:135-139 authenticates any OPEN session as principalId=sessionId with its opened capability set; agent-wrapper.ts:259-264 opens agent sessions under the operator credential with agentCapabilitiesFor(kind), which returns [ADMIN, WORK] for resource.confirm_released (vocabulary.ts:178-180), recovery.complete (:188-190) and product_contract.approve_gate_1 (:194-196). Such a session POSTs /session/pair/request (gets requestId+label), POSTs /session/pair/approve with its own credential and the label (passes :162), POSTs /session/pair/claim, and receives the mint from daemon-store-dependencies.ts:304-312: OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES = [ADMIN, GOAL, PLANNING, REVIEW, WORK] (vocabulary.ts:258-261), principalId stamped = config.operatorPrincipalId (session-handshake.ts:110), TTL 12h (session-handshake.ts:28). Renewable: session.renew is ADMIN-family (vocabulary.ts:71), not in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS (:267-279), and renewSession (session-services.ts:155-186) fences only sessionId/expiresAt/version. The minted record (opener = operator, exact five caps) also satisfies hasEventStreamOperatorAuthority (event-stream-access.ts:78-84), so the escalated agent gains the operator-only stream cursor too.

THE REPO'S OWN RULE the route breaks: vocabulary.ts:104-107 and :263-266 ("ADMIN fences REACH, not humanity ... demands the CONFIGURED operator identity no minted session can hold"), :171-177 (the explicit warning against exactly this weakening), enforced for commands at daemon-command-registry.ts:161-169 (OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION) and for the stream at event-stream-access.ts:66-85.

WHY TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT: http-listener-pairing-routes.test.ts:32-37 hardcodes principalId "operator-1" on every arm and HOSTILE_APPROVAL_CASES (:65-71) has no non-operator-principal case; http-listener-pairing-approval.test.ts:30-35 uses the fixture authenticator whose principal id never varies. Fixture is not seam: the identity fence needs the REAL createSessionAuthenticator over a real store.

CONSUMERS: git grep "pair/approve" across apps/packages/tests hits only three daemon test files. Every production approval path is terminal/private-pipe (daemon-main.ts:175, project-manager-main.ts:303/309, project-single-main.ts:149, project-stack-host.ts:110-116/212) reaching operator.approve via http-listener.ts:812-817 approvePairing or project-manager-http.ts:149. So retiring the HTTP approve route (reviewer's second option) removes the surface with no known production caller; fencing it on the operator principal (first option) is the alternative. Either closes R3-1; the DoD pins the observable, not the branch.
